description: The SignalR contract between Player.Vm.Api and its browser clients. Every name here is written twice in the estate - once in this repository and once in player/vm.ui or player/console.ui - and nothing at build or run time compares the two. Asserted against the server by src/Player.Vm.Api.Tests/ContractTests.cs and against the clients by crucible-tests/playerVm/tests/contract/signalr-contract.spec.ts. GENERATED - do not edit the structure by hand: run VMAPI_UPDATE_CONTRACTS=1 dotnet test --filter FullyQualifiedName~ContractTests, read the diff, and re-run without the variable. The descriptions, the note prose, the clients lists and clientListenersWithNoSender are carried forward untouched and are the parts to edit, along with the progress hub's broadcasts - see HubsWhoseBroadcastsAreDriven in ContractTests.cs for why that one is not derived.

broadcasts.name: VmCreated
broadcasts.note: Two arities. VmCreatedSignalRHandler goes through VmBaseSignalRHandler and sends (vm, null) because it shares the send with VmUpdated; VmTeamCreatedSignalRHandler sends (vm). A client may bind one argument and no more.

broadcasts.name: VmUpdated
broadcasts.note: (vm, modifiedProperties). The second argument is the camelCased list under modifiedProperties below.

broadcasts.name: ActiveVirtualMachine
broadcasts.note: (vmId, userId, lastSeen, teamIds). vm.ui binds all four; console.ui binds only the first, which SignalR allows - the rest are dropped on arrival.

broadcasts.name: CurrentVirtualMachineUsers
broadcasts.note: (vmId, usernames, groupId). Consumed by console.ui only.

invocations.name: Leave
invocations.note: No client calls this. A console that navigates away drops the connection instead, so the group is cleaned up by the disconnect rather than by an invocation.

broadcasts.name: Progress
broadcasts.note: The only broadcast name in the application that is not a constant: both pollers write the literal, at Domain/Vsphere/Services/TaskService.cs and Domain/Proxmox/Services/ProxmoxTaskService.cs.

clientListenersWithNoSender.name: Complete
clientListenersWithNoSender.note: Pending upstream: console.ui's notification service registers a Complete handler that clears its progress state, and no part of Player.Vm.Api ever sends it. The state is cleared by the last Progress message instead.

modifiedProperties.description: The second argument of VmUpdated. VmUpdatedSignalRHandler camelCases the property names EF's change tracker reported, and vm.ui uses each one to index the serialized Vm - model[x] = vm[x] - so a name that is not a JSON key of the DTO silently writes undefined over a live value.

neverSent.description: JSON keys of the Vm DTO with no scalar property of the Vm entity behind them, so they never appear in modifiedProperties however they change. A client that only applies what modifiedProperties names will never see these move on an update - it has to take them from the whole Vm the first argument carries.
